summary: guacd is the Apache Guacamole proxy daemon: a text-framed opcode protocol (`LENGTH.VALUE,...;`) that a Guacamole web tier calls into on 4822/tcp to open RDP/VNC/SSH/Telnet/K8s sessions on behalf of a browser client. It is **completely absent** from recce today - not in svcdetect.PORT_NAMES, not in serviceenum._PORT/_NAME, no probe module, no CVE hooks. Because guacd assumes it lives on loopback and trusts its caller, ANY reachable 4822 is a critical exposure: an attacker can send `6.select,3.rdp;` and use guacd as an RDP/VNC/SSH pivot to arbitrary hosts (an outbound SSRF over binary protocols), and the pre-1.2.0 codebase carries CVE-2020-9497/9498 (info disclosure + heap UAF -> RCE as guacd) reachable pre-auth over exactly this port. The service also self-identifies its version in the `args` reply (VERSION_1_5_0 etc.) so version-keyed CVE mapping is cheap. Proposed module recce/services/guacamole.py mirrors the vnc.py shape: one TCP roundtrip per opcode, stdlib-only, 4s timeout, air-gap safe.

existing_coverage.notes: grep for 'guac' or '4822' across recce/ returns zero hits (excluding vendored node_modules). Not in svcdetect.py PORT_NAMES (line 34-77), not in serviceenum.py _NAME or _PORT (line 11-49), no signature in _SIGNATURES (line 88-105), no product regex in _PRODUCT_RE (line 121-141), no per-service script under recce/scripts/, no runbook, no CVE hook.

cross_service_wire_candidates: guacd version token (VERSION_1_x_y from `args` reply) -> feeds CVE mapper for CVE-2020-9497/9498 keyed on Apache Guacamole <1.2.0 (chain into recce/services/probes.py CVE emit path used by http/rdp/etc.)

Enumerated backend protocols (rdp/vnc/ssh/telnet/kubernetes/mysql/postgresql/sftp reported as supported by the guacd binary via `select` accept/reject) -> hints to rdp.py / vnc.py / ssh.py that the *target* environment expects those services somewhere; more importantly signals that guacd itself can be weaponised as an outbound SSRF proxy for those protocols

Presence of guacd on a host -> strong sibling-port hint for http/web enum: the Guacamole web tier almost always co-locates on 8080/tcp or 8443/tcp at path /guacamole/ (Tomcat). Wire a hint to recce/services/web/ to probe /guacamole/#/ and the /guacamole/api/tokens login endpoint with default creds guacadmin:guacadmin (a known default-cred hit).

Non-loopback bind on 4822 -> feeds attack-path graph: guacd is an unauthenticated pivot into the internal network for RDP/VNC/SSH targets - the cred-quickconnect / exploit-session-wiring path can use it to reach hosts otherwise unreachable from the tester's segment.
Server framing (opcode `args`) captured as banner -> feeds svcdetect._SIGNATURES so any *other* port a defender re-homed guacd onto still classifies correctly.
Absent-args or 'error,' opcode reply distinguishing hardened builds -> feeds fingerprint confidence tier for the Findings sheet.

capabilities.name: Register 4822/tcp in svcdetect PORT_NAMES
capabilities.description: Add `4822: ('guacd', 'Apache Guacamole proxy daemon')` to recce/services/svcdetect.py PORT_NAMES so a bare/unknown 4822 gets an inferred label with detect_source='inferred'. Zero traffic.
capabilities.notes: Also add to serviceenum.py _PORT (4822: 'guacamole') and _NAME ('guacd': 'guacamole', 'guacamole': 'guacamole') so `recce services` prints a next-command.

capabilities.name: guacd instruction-framing signature in _SIGNATURES
capabilities.description: Add a regex like `^\d+\.args,\d+\.VERSION_\d+_\d+_\d+,` (matches the guacd `args` frame with an embedded VERSION_x_y_z token) to svcdetect._SIGNATURES so any banner we grab - on 4822 or anywhere else guacd got re-homed - classifies as guacamole with detect_source='banner'.
capabilities.notes: Must be latin-1 safe; guacd frames are 7-bit ASCII so the regex is trivial.

capabilities.name: Product/version extraction for CVE keying
capabilities.description: Add a _PRODUCT_RE entry that captures prod='Apache Guacamole' and ver from the VERSION_1_5_0 -> '1.5.0' token in an `args` reply, so port.product/port.version populate for the existing CVE mapper without a bespoke code path.
capabilities.notes: Regex: r'VERSION_(?P<ver_raw>\d+_\d+_\d+)' with a post-process s/_/./g and prod='Apache Guacamole' assigned literally.

capabilities.name: Active guacd protocol probe (select handshake)
capabilities.description: New recce/services/guacamole.py::probe(ip, port=4822, timeout=4). Connect, send `6.select,3.vnc;` (12 bytes on the wire), read the `args` frame, parse the LENGTH.VALUE,... instruction, extract version + argument names. Returns {reachable, version, backends_ok:[], backends_err:[], args_seen:[]}. Mirrors vnc.py::probe shape and uses svcprobe.iter_probe for budget/progress/state.
capabilities.notes: Framing helper: encode = lambda *els: ','.join(f'{len(e)}.{e}' for e in els) + ';'. Decode a single instruction with a small state machine reading LENGTH then '.' then VALUE-of-that-many-chars then ',' or ';'.

capabilities.name: Backend-protocol enumeration
capabilities.description: For each candidate `select,<proto>` in {rdp, vnc, ssh, telnet, kubernetes, sftp, mysql, postgresql}, open a fresh TCP connection, issue the select, and record whether guacd replies with `args` (backend built in) or an `error` frame / immediate close (backend disabled or protocol plugin missing). Populates probe['backends_ok'] and drives the exposure finding's blast radius.
capabilities.protocol_reference: Guacamole protocol reference - the initial `select` opcode; supported protocols listed in Guacamole User Guide chapter 'Connecting to your server'.
capabilities.notes: Rate-limit: 1 opcode per second baseline; 8 opcodes total for the full sweep. Reuse svcprobe.iter_probe for budget control.

capabilities.name: Finding: guacd_exposed (CRITICAL, no-auth pivot)
capabilities.description: Emit CRITICAL when probe.reachable is true from a non-loopback source: guacd has no authentication - the web tier is expected to authenticate the user and then proxy to guacd on 127.0.0.1. A reachable 4822 lets an attacker issue arbitrary `select,rdp` with any hostname argument and use guacd as an outbound RDP/VNC/SSH proxy into anywhere guacd can route.
capabilities.notes: Detail should quote the offered backends so the tester sees the pivot surface (rdp+ssh = full lateral).

capabilities.name: Finding: guacd_cve_2020_9498 (RCE, HIGH)
capabilities.description: Emit HIGH when parsed version < 1.2.0. CVE-2020-9498 is a heap use-after-free in guacd's RDP client (guac_common_svc_process_receive) reachable pre-auth over 4822 that yields code execution as the guacd user.
capabilities.notes: Chain with guacd_exposed: exposed + <1.2.0 = pre-auth RCE, upgrade severity note in detail.

capabilities.name: Finding: guacd_cve_2020_9497 (info disclosure, MEDIUM)
capabilities.description: Emit MEDIUM when parsed version < 1.2.0. CVE-2020-9497 leaks uninitialised memory from the guacd process through a crafted static virtual channel packet - useful for extracting session tokens / adjacent connection material.

capabilities.name: Finding: guacd_fingerprint (info)
capabilities.description: Always emit an info finding on a reachable guacd carrying version + accepted-backends list, matching the vnc_fingerprint pattern. Gives the sheet a stable row per target even when no CVE fires.

capabilities.name: Runbook: credentialed + cred-free next steps
capabilities.description: runbook(ip, port) returns a two-lane list matching vnc.py::runbook: cred-free lane is `nc <ip> 4822` + a paste-able `printf '6.select,3.vnc;'`; escalated lane is a pointer to the co-located /guacamole/ web UI on 8080/8443 with default creds guacadmin:guacadmin.
capabilities.notes: No `guacenc` invocation - that's an offline recording tool, not a client.

capabilities.description: Add scripts/guacamole to run the probe + enum against a single target from the shell driver, and register 'guacamole' in scripts/recce-service.sh's name_to_svc / port_to_svc maps (kept in sync with serviceenum.py per the module docstring).

capabilities.name: findings_to_vulns integration
capabilities.description: Add `findings_to_vulns(fs) -> dict` in guacamole.py that delegates to svccommon.findings_to_vulns(fs, 'guacamole', 4822), mirroring vnc.py:179-181, so guacd findings surface in the vulns aggregator + attack-path graph.

capabilities.name: analyze() orchestrator (public entry)
capabilities.description: Top-level `analyze(hosts, creds, active, budget, progress)` that lists guacd_targets, runs probe via svcprobe.iter_probe when active, calls findings(), returns {targets, findings, runbooks, probes, stats} - identical shape to vnc.py::analyze(184-205) so the existing services runner picks it up with no bespoke wiring.

capabilities.name: suggest_id_command hint for still-unknown 4822
capabilities.description: Extend svcdetect.suggest_id_command so an unknown 4822 emits `printf '6.select,3.vnc;' | nc <ip> 4822   # guacd - expect an args, frame` instead of the generic nmap suggestion. Turns 'unknown 4822' into a one-liner ID.
capabilities.notes: Small edit to svcdetect.py::suggest_id_command around line 392.

capabilities.name: TLS variant handling (guacd-ssl / self-signed)
capabilities.description: When plaintext probe reads 0 bytes on 4822 and TLS is offered (some hardened installs enable guacd-ssl.crt/guacd-ssl.key with `enable-ssl: true` in guacd.conf), fall through to a TLS handshake + `select` retry, matching the tls_http_probe pattern already in svcdetect.py:218-246.

capabilities.name: Cross-wire: emit http-hint for /guacamole/ web tier
capabilities.description: When guacd is confirmed reachable, publish a hint into the shared host-facts channel (the same mechanism msrpc/kerberos use to seed downstream modules) that http/https on the same host should be probed with URL hint /guacamole/ and creds guacadmin:guacadmin. That is the productised entry point - the web tier is where credential attacks land, and guacd's presence is the strongest single signal that a /guacamole/ context exists.
capabilities.notes: Concretely: append {'ip': ip, 'path': '/guacamole/', 'creds': [('guacadmin','guacadmin')], 'kind': 'guacamole_web'} to host.hints for the web enum module to consume.
